Approved evidence

APEX-v1

benchmark.apex-v1

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

The original APEX-v1.0 primary paper and the independently pinned creator APEX-v1-extended card describe one explicitly versioned APEX task/evaluation lineage. Three separate AI source-content review invocations bind each approved assertion at its exact scientific digest. Original hidden/public partitions, model/response/grader conditions, later extended protocol, source denominators and incompatible-looking use/license statements stay qualified. This is the retained finite-inventory APEX-1 target, newly admitted to this graph; it is distinct from the already recorded APEX-Agents and APEX Accounting families. No replicated results, current supplier performance assessment, source-document rights clearance, family duplication or finalized core eligibility is asserted.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

APEX-v1 · recruited: For APEX-v1.0, Mercor sourced experienced professionals, interviewed them for 30-45 minutes, and paid selected experts to complete a 1-2 hour prompt-and-rubric assessment before successful applicants were contracted.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.apex.family.expert-selection-and-contracting.v4

  • The authors prioritized appropriate industry experience and prior data-labeling experience, and continued qualitative feedback with offboarding when needed.
  • This is the paper's account of expert recruitment and contracted benchmark production; the recruitment account does not state an hourly pay rate.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

APEX-v1 · human annotation: APEX-v1.0 experts first described 3-5 common daily-work tasks and their required seniority, then used that workflow input to create prompts and find or create supporting evidence sources.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.apex.family.expert-task-and-source-production.v4

  • Sources could be PDFs or CSVs with combined length at most 100,000 tokens, checked with OpenAI's GPT 4o tokenizer; the paper notes that experts created sources when suitable free material was unavailable, such as patient records.
  • Appendix C workflow time allocations are estimates from experts' survey responses, rather than measured time allocations for a representative occupational population.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

APEX-v1 · access terms: The pinned APEX-v1-extended card labels the release CC-BY 4.0 while also stating exclusive evaluation use and forbidding training, fine-tuning, parameter fitting, crawling and scraping.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.apex.family.extended-card-license-and-use-statements.v3

  • Its further robots-exclusion statement asks users not to programmatically download the dataset or use it for automated processing without express permission.
  • The card presents its scenarios as hypothetical research material rather than actual contemplated transactions or professional advice.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

APEX-v1 · documents: The captured APEX-v1-extended creator card describes 400 heldout tasks, 100 per job, plus 100 open-source development tasks; it replaces the original three-judge panel with Gemini 2.5 Pro thinking On as a single judge.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.apex.family.extended-version-protocol.v3

  • The extended card specifies eight responses per task and mean aggregation, with the prompt and source documents supplied to the judge alongside the rubric.
  • These are the extended card's release and protocol statements, distinct from the pinned paper's 200-case, three-response, three-judge APEX-v1.0 experiment.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

APEX-v1 · access terms: The original APEX-v1.0 paper describes a closed heldout evaluation set and publishes four example prompts with rubrics that were created by the same expert group under the same instructions but are outside that heldout set.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.apex.family.heldout-and-public-examples.v3

  • The authors retain the test set as hidden to reduce contamination while acknowledging that disclosure of its design means contamination cannot be fully ruled out.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

APEX-v1 · benchmark task: The paper's original APEX-v1.0 collection has 200 cases, 50 each for investment banking, management consulting, law and medicine, created and reviewed by industry experts.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.apex.family.original-expert-case-collection.v4

  • The authors report 76 contributors who each supplied at least one case, with mean professional experience of 7.25 years, sourced through the Mercor platform.
  • Each case pairs a prompt with evidence sources and a prompt-specific quality rubric.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

APEX-v1 · adjudicated: APEX-v1.0 reviews prompts before contributors write the corresponding rubrics, then reviews those rubrics through potentially multiple rounds; 200 of 300 started prompts were approved for the final collection.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.apex.family.staged-human-quality-control.v3

  • Experts begin as contributors and can be promoted to reviewers after exceptional performance and demonstrated understanding of requirements.
  • In-house LM tools supply immediate reviewing feedback, while the human experts remain responsible for submission quality.
